both CpG methylation and activation induced deaminases are required for the fragility of the human bcl 2 MBR.

the AID enzyme creates lesions that are dependent on CpG methylation at the MBR and that the phosphodiester bond breakage at the MBR lesions are dependent on the Artemis enzyme, which has been shown to be capable of nicking mismatches and heteroduplexes, including single base mismatches.
both AID induced DNA lesions and DNA methylation are required to explain the propensity of the bcl 1 major breakpoint region to break at CpG sites.

the mechanisms of the t(14, 18) translocations and the role of the AID enzyme in those mechanisms.
the timing of the chromosome 18 breaks that cause human follicular B cell lymphoma.
the mechanisms that cause the MBR breaks in the t( 14; 18) chromosomal transaction that is responsible for the vast majority of human follicular lymphomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both DNA methylation and the AID enzyme are essential for MBR breakage, and that Artemis, in addition to RAG, is essential for the MBR break.

the MBR breaks in t(14; 18) are highly dependent on CpG methylation, and that the AID enzyme is required to generate the MBR lesions, and that Artemis is required to nick the lesions to generate the chromosome breaks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both CpG methylation and AID are required for the fragility of the MBR and the breaks in the t( 14;18) translocation.

both CpG methylation and AID are essential elements of a theory for the fragility of the MBR, but the actual nicks in the MBR DNA are made by Artemis, a DNA repair enzyme that normally acts at the IgH gene.

AID and Artemis are both required for the fragility of the MBR, and this provides a mechanism for how the t(14,18) breaks occur at precisely the same time.
